title: Singular and plural marking tracks the counted participant set
summary: A speculative number-agreement hypothesis assigns singular/plural form to the cardinality of one selected participant set, rather than to a lexical category or arbitrary record style.

design.unit: records with a counted participant set and a candidate singular/plural form
design.contrast: participant cardinality agreement versus lexical category marking
design.prediction: Holding lexical category and record type fixed, changing the selected participant count from one to multiple should switch the form; changing an unselected neighboring set should not.
design.countermodel: The same surface alternation could reflect editorial batch conventions, lexicalized forms, or analyst counting choices without either proposed semantic rule.
design.falsifier: The form stays fixed when the selected count changes, or switches when only an unselected set changes under matched scope.
design.principal_risk: Independent participant counts and number meanings are unavailable. Near IDEA000064 argument agreement and historical flower-count material, but targets cardinality of a designated set rather than a modifier’s argument class or a lexical category.
